To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
economic reforms in Ghana have been characterized by poor macroeconomic policy sequencing.

(i) the economic reform programmes of the 1980s have achieved some stabilization and growth, but (ii) agricultural development has been disappointing and (iii) macro policy sequencing has been poor, with the result that the agricultural sector has suffered.
economic reform programmes are likely to succeed when they are sequenced in an order that is mutually enhancing, that is, when demand management measures are set within structural measures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sequencing of policy measures in economic reform programmes and their implications for growth and development, with special emphasis on agriculture.
the sequencing of macro policy reforms, particularly in respect to the role of agriculture.

the following: (1) the extent to which economic reforms were achieved; (2) the extent to and reasons why agricultural growth and development were achieved; and (3) the extent to, and reasons why the reform programmes were sustained.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reform programme has been a success.
the reform programme was not a failure, but that it did not succeed as it should have.
the economic programme was a success in the sense of stabilizing the economy and laying a foundation for growth and development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

economic reform programmes can succeed in Ghana if there is a clear sequencing of macroeconomic policies, and if there is an understanding of social dimensions of economic reform and a commitment to ameliorate social costs of adjustment.
economic reforms are not ends but means to an end.
the economic reform programmes in Ghana have not been as successful as expected, but that they have not been as unsuccessful as feared.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the macro policy sequencing of economic reform programmes is an important determinant of the success or otherwise of economic reforms.
macroeconomic policies must be sequenced in an orderly manner to achieve the desired results.
macro policy sequencing is an important factor in the achievement of sustainable development.
